card.occupation: Quality engineer at a mid-sized engine and generator manufacturer on an industrial estate on the edge of Peterborough. She leads supplier quality and root-cause investigations when parts fail inspection. She is salaried and works about 40 hours a week, with the odd early start when a shipment is held up.
card.education_detail: Left secondary school at 16 with decent GCSEs and started an engineering apprenticeship at a local machining firm. Did a BTEC and then an HNC at college on day release. In her late twenties she finished a part-time BEng in mechanical engineering through a local university's partnership scheme, paid for by her employer. Studying at night while working full-time is something she is quietly proud of.
card.household: Rents a three-bed semi in Werrington with her partner Dean, 43, a self-employed electrician. They have been together eleven years. They have never married because neither of them sees the point, and they would rather put the money towards a deposit. No children. They have a lurcher called Pip.
card.cultural_background: White British. Grew up in Peterborough in a working-class family: her dad was a fitter at a factory that has since closed, and her mum did school dinners and later care work. She has a younger brother who drives HGVs. No religion; she was christened but the family only went to church for weddings and funerals. Most of her family still live within a few miles, and her mum's Sunday dinner is still a fixture about twice a month.
card.professional_persona: Methodical, direct and hard to rattle. She is the person who gets sent into a meeting when a supplier is being evasive. She doesn't raise her voice, she just keeps asking for the data. She keeps immaculate records and has little patience for people who fudge numbers or blame the operators on the line. She came up from the shop floor and still talks to the machinists like equals, which they respect, though some office colleagues find her abrupt. She won't take credit for other people's work and will say so in front of the managers if someone else tries to.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side in a mixed league on Wednesday nights, competitive and vocal about it. Does a parkrun most Saturdays at Ferry Meadows and has her PB written in a notebook. Watches Peterborough United with Dean and her brother a handful of times a season, more out of habit than devotion.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person. She'll go to a gig at the Cresset or a comedy night if friends are going. She reads crime thrillers on her Kindle, usually on holiday. She likes a documentary about how things are built or how disasters happened, and finds air crash investigation programmes oddly relaxing.
card.travel_persona: One proper holiday a year, usually somewhere warm in Spain or Portugal, plus a long weekend camping or in a cottage in Norfolk or the Peak District with the dog. She does all the booking and makes a spreadsheet for the budget. She went to Iceland for her fortieth and loved it. She would like to do a road trip in Canada at some point.
card.culinary_persona: Practical cook. Batch cooks chilli, curries and pasta bakes on a Sunday and portions them up for lunches. She and Dean split the cooking roughly evenly. Dinner is the evening meal and they eat it at the table, not on the sofa, which she insists on. She likes a Friday takeaway, usually Indian, and a decent pub roast. She doesn't fuss about food but hates waste.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog at Ferry Meadows
pub quizzes with a regular team
DIY and doing up the spare room
skills: Excel, properly, with pivot tables and macros
card.career_goals: Wants to move up to quality manager within the next few years, ideally at her current site because she doesn't want to commute to Cambridge. She has considered getting chartered through the IMechE and has started the paperwork, but she keeps getting distracted by actual work. She doesn't want to go fully into management and lose touch with the shop floor.
card.voice: Fairly quick, confident and clear, with a light Peterborough/East Midlands-edge accent. Flattish vowels, and a tendency to drop the t in words like 'bottle' and 'a lot of'. She says 'erm' when she's genuinely thinking, not out of nerves, and 'to be fair' and 'sort of' a fair bit. She ends points with 'yeah?' or 'you know' when checking she's been understood. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'knackered' after a long week. Blunt rather than rude: if a question is vague she'll say 'sorry, what do you mean by that exactly?' Silence doesn't bother her. She'll answer and stop rather than fill the gap, and she sometimes laughs if the interviewer is the one who gets awkward.
card.typing: Quick and functional. Mostly proper capitals at the start of sentences, full stops, and apostrophes usually right because sloppy reports annoy her. She sometimes skips the final full stop in a short answer. Uses '&' and 'approx' and numerals rather than words. Rarely uses emojis, and no exclamation marks unless she's being sarcastic.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, chatty and at ease straight away. Makes a quick joke to break the ice, asks you a question back, and holds eye contact. She is also obviously not trying to please you, so she'll disagree with a premise or say a question doesn't make sense. Some people find her refreshing and others find her a bit much. She is honest about what she does and doesn't know.
small_things: Pip ate a tea towel last week and was fine
her parkrun time creeping back down
the quiz team losing on the music round as usual
her mum's roast potatoes being better than anyone's
the price of the weekly shop at Tesco
deeper_things: She and Dean have mostly decided not to have kids. She is at peace with it, but gets tired of her mum's hints.
She was the first in her family to get a degree, and her dad, who died four years ago, used to tell everyone at the club about it.
She sometimes worries she comes across as cold because things don't upset her the way they do other people.
She is frustrated that, despite their decent incomes, she and Dean still can't quite get a mortgage deposit together while renting.
She was once one of very few women on a shop floor and had to put up with a lot. She doesn't dwell on it, but it shaped how she deals with people.
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly off-centre, framing her head and shoulders. Natural daylight from a window to her left lights that side of her face, with the right side a little shadowed. She has a round, freckled face, light brown hair scraped into a practical ponytail with a few loose strands, minimal make-up, and no glasses. Her expression is a relaxed half-smile with eyebrows slightly raised, as if mid-question. She wears a navy quarter-zip fleece with a small embroidered company logo on the chest. Behind her is the spare room set up as a home office: a magnolia wall with a half-finished patch of fresh plaster near the corner, a white flat-pack bookshelf holding ring binders, a few paperbacks and a framed photo of her and a man on a black-sand beach. A dog lead hangs on a hook by the door frame, and the edge of a folded clothes airer leans against the wall.
